newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Durian demand boost for Cathay 747 freight.
newsitem.headline: Durian demand boost for Cathay 747 freight.

text.p: Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd has begun flying large amounts of durian from Bangkok to meet the demand of fruit lovers in Hong Kong, the airline's cargo marketing and sales manager Ray Jewell said.

In addition to belly cargo on passenger services, two ad hoc Cathay Boeing 747-200 freighter flights were arranged this week and one last week, with more expected until the durian season finishes at end-May, he told Reuters.
The famously pungent spiky, football shaped durian fruit is dubbed Thailand's 'king of fruits' and is exported in large quantities to connoisseurs' dining tables.

Demand for ad hoc freighter flights to carry durians has declined recently as newly arrived passenger aircraft such as the Boeing 777 and the Airbus A330 have a much larger belly cargo capacity than Cathay's now retired Lockheed Tristar regional fleet.
Rival airlines also investing in modern cargo friendly aircraft has been another factor, Jewell added. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
